To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned and characterized genes involved in elloramycin biosynthesis in Streptomyces.
the biosynthesis of the elloramycin antibiotic is controlled by the polyketide synthetase genes elmPKS1-elmPKS5.
the genes of the polyketides tetracenomycins and elloramycin were cloned from Streptomyce olivaceus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of genes from the tetracycline producer Streptomyces aureofaciens, the tetracenromycin producer Streptomyce olivaceus and the polyene macrolide producer Streptomycess lividans.
the isolation, characterization and expression of the genes involved in the biosynthesis of ELM in S. olivaceus.

the cloning of the genes for the biosynthesis of the polyketides tetracenomycins, erythromycin and ELM from S. aureofaciens (Sa) ATCC 10762, Saccharopolyspora erythraea (Se) ATCC 11635 and S. olivaceus ATCC 3110, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gene cluster for the biosynthesis of ELM is located on a 40-kb fragment of the So Tü2354 chromosome.
the genes for the ELM biosynthetic pathway have been identified and characterized, and a gene cluster for ELM production has been cloned.
the genes for elloramycin biosynthesis are located on cosmid 16 F4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the genes required for the production of ELM from So Tü235
the genes responsible for the production of ELM from So Tü2354 are present on cosmid 16 F4.
the ELM gene cluster is located in the 16F4 region and is flanked by two transposon-like elements, one at each end of 16F4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to identify and clone genes from S. olivaceus involved in ELM biosynthesis using a tetracenomycincosynthetase (TcmO) gene probe from the TCM biosynthetic pathway.
we have identified the genes for elloramycin biosynthesis in S. olivaceus, and we have demonstrated that the biosynthetic machinery for ELM and tetracenomycins are similar.
the ELM biosynthetic pathway is similar to the tetracenomicyn biosynthetic pathway, and that the genes involved in the biosynthesis of the tetracenominycin and ELM are closely related.
